He played college basketball for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] before being drafted 21st overall by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Fagan |first=Ryan |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-03-07/dukes-nolan-smith-our-big-guys-have-definitely-gotten-better |title=Duke's Nolan Smith: 'Our big guys have definitely gotten better' |work=SportingNews.com |date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=March 21, 2010 |archive-date=December 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204135546/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-03-07/dukes-nolan-smith-our-big-guys-have-definitely-gotten-better |url-status=dead }} As a junior, he started at shooting guard for Duke's [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|national champion]] [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010 team]]. As a senior, he was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]]. ==Early life== As a child, Smith frequently attended [[Washington Bullets]] practices after his father, then-former NBA player, [[Derek Smith (basketball)|Derek Smith]], took their assistant coach position in 1994. Following the death of his father in 1996, the Bullets made Smith a frequent guest at their home games.{{cite web|last=Dinich |first=Heather |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?id=3196773 |title=Nolan Smith keeps the memory of his father close |work=ESPN.com |date=January 16, 2008 |access-date=November 30, 2014}} ==High school career== As an eighth grader, Smith played varsity basketball for [[The Key School]] in [[Annapolis, Maryland]] before moving to [[St. John's College High School]] in Washington, D.C. for his freshman season in 2003–04. At St. John's, he was a third-team all-conference pick while averaging 10.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.1 steals per game.{{cite web| url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=1211262& |title=Nolan Smith Bio |work=GoDuke.com |access-date=November 30, 2014}} As a sophomore in 2004–05, Smith attended [[Riverdale Baptist School]] in [[Upper Marlboro, Maryland]]. There, he averaged 16 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals per game as he led Riverdale to a 33–1 record and subsequently earned third-team All-Metro honors. For his junior and senior years, Smith attended [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]] where he was a two-year captain and played alongside several future NBA players, including [[Michael Beasley]], [[Ty Lawson]] and [[Brandon Jennings]]. In 2005–06, he averaged 17 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals per game as he helped Oak Hill to a 40–1 overall record and a final ''USA Today'' No. 2 national ranking. He subsequently earned EA Sports second-team All-America honors. On November 13, 2006, Smith signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for [[Duke University]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=684673 |title=Blue Devils Ink Three During Early Signing Period |work=GoDuke.com |date=November 13, 2006 |access-date=November 30, 2014}} As a senior in 2006–07, Smith averaged 22.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 3.2 steals per game as he led his team to a 40–1 record, tying the school's single season wins record and helping Oak Hill earn the top spot in the final ''USA Today'' 2007 Super 25 national rankings. He earned first-team EA Sports and [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] honors and was named to the Les Schwab Invitational all-tournament team after leading Oak Hill to the championship. He also earned [[2007 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]] honors. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Smith was listed as the No. 8 shooting guard and the No. 39 player in the nation in 2007.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Nolan-Smith-30073;_ylt=AhLgWJiXtlnUop_8biZWMXpGPZB4 Nolan Smith Recruiting Profile] ==College career== ===Freshman year=== As a freshman at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in 2007–08, Smith played in all 34 games, with one starting assignment as he averaged 5.9 points, 1.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 14.7 minutes per game. He earned his first collegiate start against Cornell on January 6, 2008, and scored nine points on 4-of-6 shooting, while overall, he scored in double figures six times, including a season-high 21 points against Wake Forest on February 17. ===Sophomore year=== As a sophomore in 2008–09, Smith played in 34 games, with 21 starting assignments as he averaged 8.4 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. He finished the season ranked fourth on the team in double-figure scoring games with 17. He scored a season-high 16 points, along with five rebounds and four assists, against Michigan on November 21, 2008. ===Junior year=== As a junior in 2009–10, Smith started 38 games after sitting out the first two games of the season, serving a suspension for playing in a non-sanctioned summer league game. He averaged 17.4 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He led the Blue Devils in field goals made; finished second in assists, steals and three-point field goal percentage; and third on the team in scoring, three-point field goals, free throws made, free throw percentage and minutes. He subsequently earned second-team All-ACC honors, and claimed USBWA All-District III and NABC Second Team All-District 2 honors. March 28, 2010, Smith scored a then career-high 29 points on 9-of-17 from the field in an [[Elite Eight]] game, as Duke defeated Baylor and advanced to the [[Final Four]]. In that game, Smith (628 points), [[Jon Scheyer]] (690 points) and [[Kyle Singler]] (667 points) became the second trio in Duke history to each score at least 600 points in a season; in 2001–02, [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]], [[Carlos Boozer]] and [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]] first accomplished that feat for Duke.{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040 |title=Notes: Duke 78, Baylor 71 |work=GoDuke.com |date=March 28, 2010 |access-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-date=December 5, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205091943/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040 |url-status=dead }} Smith went on to earn NCAA All-Final Four team as he led Duke to an [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA championship]] victory. He averaged 16 points and five assists per game in wins over West Virginia and Butler. ===Senior year=== [[File:Nolan Smith vs Miami.jpg|thumb|left|alt=Duke Blue Devils guard Nolan Smith (2) drive past Miami Hurricanes guard Durand Scott (1) during the game between Miami and Duke at Bank United Center in Coral Gables, Florida.|Nolan (2) was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] in 2011.]] As a senior in 2010–11, Smith started 37 games as he averaged 20.6 points, 4.5 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web| url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/nolan-smith-1.html |title=Nolan Smith Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=November 30, 2014}} He was named the 12th ACC Player of the Year in school history after becoming the 11th Duke player to lead the league in scoring. He earned first-team All-ACC and ACC All-Defensive team honors, and NABC and USBWA first-team All-District honors after leading Duke to a 32–5 record and a third consecutive ACC championship. He was also a finalist for the Naismith Trophy, Wooden Award, Oscar Robertson Trophy and Bob Cousy Award. On February 9, 2011, Smith scored a career high 34 points in a home win over No. 20 North Carolina, making a career-high 13 field goal attempts. Smith was the team captain in 2010–11, along with fellow senior [[Kyle Singler]]. He was well respected amongst his peers as teammates gravitated towards him in the locker room because of his passion for the game, and his ability to remain energetic and loose in high-pressure situations. He became just the ninth player under [[Mike Krzyzewski]] to average over 20.0 points per game, and with his 764 total points in 2010–11, he recorded the ninth highest single season total and is just the 19th time a Duke player has scored 700 or more. ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2011–2013)=== [[File:Damian Lillard and Nolan Smith.jpg|thumb|right|Smith (right) with teammate [[Damian Lillard]] in 2013]] Smith was selected with the 21st overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. On December 9, 2011, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web |url=http://www.wbir.com/news/article/195087/0/Blazers-rookie-Smith-signs |title=Blazers rookie Smith signs |work=WBIR.com |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=November 30, 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141130142534/http://www.wbir.com/news/article/195087/0/Blazers-rookie-Smith-signs |archive-date=November 30, 2014 |url-status=dead }} As a rookie, he played 44 games (four starts) and averaged 3.8 points, 1.4 assists and 1.3 rebounds in 12.3 minutes per game. In July 2012, Smith joined the Trail Blazers for the 2012 [[NBA Summer League]], but managed just two games after he was ruled out for the rest of the competition on July 17 when he received an elbow to the head from Rockets' swingman [[Zoran Dragić]] while driving to the hoop. He was carried out on a stretcher and the game was called off with 27 seconds left to play. Later that day, after tests came back normal, he was released from Las Vegas hospital.{{cite news|title=Allen: Nolan Smith Likely Out For Remainder Of Summer League|url=http://forwardcenter.net/allen-nolan-smith-likely-out-for-remainder-of-summer-league/|date=July 17, 2012|access-date=November 30, 2014|work=ForwardCenter.net|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304040846/http://forwardcenter.net/allen-nolan-smith-likely-out-for-remainder-of-summer-league/|url-status=dead}} On January 6, 2013, Smith was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=BARTON, SMITH ASSIGNED TO STAMPEDE FROM BLAZERS|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/nolan_smith_will_barton_assign_2013_01_06.html|date=January 6, 2013|access-date=November 30, 2014|work=NBA.com}} On January 9, he was recalled by the Trail Blazers after competing in both of Idaho's games at the 2013 NBA D-League Showcase in [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]]. 2016|url-status=dead}} ==Coaching career== Following his playing career, Smith joined the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] coaching staff under head coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]]. After being hired in February 2016, Smith spent two years as a special assistant and three years as director of basketball operations & player development. In 2021, he was named a Duke assistant coach. In six years on the Duke coaching staff, the team won 159 of 206 games. In 2022, the team made the Final Four. During those six years, Smith helped coach a total of 25 players who went on to the NBA, including the following first-round draft picks: [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Luke Kennard]], [[Harry Giles III|Harry Giles]], [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Wendell Carter Jr]], [[Grayson Allen]], [[Zion Williamson]], [[R.J. Barrett]], [[Cam Reddish]], [[Jalen Johnson]], [[Paolo Banchero]], [[Mark Williams (basketball)|Mark Williams]], [[AJ Griffin (basketball)|AJ Griffin]], and [[Wendell Moore Jr.|Wendell Moore]].{{Cite web |url=http://dukereport.com/alumni/nolan-smith-joins-staff-as-special-assistant-dis/ |title=Nolan Smith Joins Staff as Special Assistant |access-date=March 19, 2016 |archive-date=March 29, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329091955/http://dukereport.com/alumni/nolan-smith-joins-staff-as-special-assistant-dis/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite web | title=Nolan Smith joins Duke coaching staff as special assistant | website=The Duke Chronicle | date=2016-02-22 | url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2016/02/nolan-smith-joins-duke-coaching-staff-as-special-assistant | access-date=2026-04-23}}{{cite web |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/nolan-smith/4163 |title=Nolan Smith - Assistant Coach - Men's Basketball Coaches |publisher=[[Duke University]] |accessdate=2022-04-05 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218021720/https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/nolan-smith/4163 |archive-date=2022-02-18}} Following the 2021–22 season, Smith left Duke to become an assistant coach for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]] under their new head coach [[Kenny Payne]].{{Cite tweet |user=goodmanhoops |number=1511051821061713922 |title=BREAKING: Duke assistant Nolan Smith is headed to Louisville to join Kenny Payne on staff, source told @Stadium |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=Twitter |language=en}} Payne had known Smith's father, [[Derek Smith (basketball)|Derek Smith]], who had starred for the [[1979–80 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville's 1980 championship team]] before a nine-year career in the NBA. He has one older sister, Sydney Smith. His father played basketball at Louisville and was a member of the 1980 NCAA championship team that defeated UCLA. His father then played nine years in the NBA. At age 34, Derek died of a heart attack while he and his family were on a cruise ship near Bermuda. Smith has a [[tattoo]] on his right arm, with his father's likeness and the words: "Forever Watching."{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Gordie|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/basketball-philadelphia-sixers/nolan-smith-knows-his-father-derek-forever-watching |title=Nolan Smith knows his father Derek is forever watching |work=CSNPhilly.com |date=March 19, 2013 |access-date=November 30, 2014}} He grew up with [[Michael Beasley]] and remains friends with him. In 2021, Nolan began co-hosting the "Power Check Ball" [https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/power-check-ball/id1572131357 podcast] alongside Marc Isenberg.{{cite web|last=Rego|first=Max|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2021/08/nolan-smith-marc-isenberg-podcast-power-check-ball-nil |title=Nolan Smith launches podcast on social justice and sports |work=dukechronicle.com |date=August 9, 2021 |access-date=June 28, 2022}} Smith is married to UNC alumna Cheyna Elliott.
